analysis:
Both units are unchanged BASE text of docs/threat-model.yaml, lines 898-1873: T-010 tail, T-011 through T-016, T-027 through T-029, T-041 with its full SSD cache posture, T-033 through T-037, T-042, T-043 and T-044 through T-046. The file_changes range map is marked complete. It lists no base-side changes. All changes are head-side insertions:
- lines 43-45: header note on the add-on hold review;
- lines 232-241: new asset A-018 provider_serving_availability;
- lines 811-841: new trust boundary TB-012 provider_to_local_addon_hold_socket;
- lines 2305-2337: presumably T-059.
None of these insertions fall inside the reviewed base ranges. I therefore found no edits, weakening or removal of existing mitigations for T-011, T-012, T-014, T-015, T-041, T-033, T-034, T-036, T-042 or T-043/T-044 in these units.
New surface, visible only through the truncated patch excerpt:
- A same-user, owner-only AF_UNIX socket lets a separately signed add-on (io.darkbloom.sandbox) make the provider withhold inference. The header names a signature check, leases and a machine-lock fallback.
- A-018 sensitivity is medium, and the impact is availability only (it affects the coordinator's routing view through heartbeat busy fields).
For integration, examine head lines 811-841 and 2305-2337, and ProviderCore/Addon/ProviderLoop+AddonHold.swift (code not supplied), and check:
- The hold path must never expose A-001 plaintext, keys (A-003) or authorization state (A-016).
- Peer signature verification should use code-signing credentials such as an audit token or designated requirement, not the PID or path. This mirrors the T-044 helper pinning.
- Lease expiry and the machine-lock fallback must not let a stale hold permanently deroute the provider, and must not let an expired hold resume while VMs are live.
- Busy fields must not be treated as trust signals by the coordinator. Coordinator handling is declared as separate platform work, so that contract is unverified.
A malicious same-user process forcing a hold is operator-controlled DoS consistent with ADV-001 and TB-003, not a confidentiality regression. No findings are supported from these base units.
